title: Cuban Black Beans with Red Pepper Sofrito
summary: Slow-simmered black beans turn silky and deeply flavoured with a garlicky red pepper sofrito, finished with a bright hit of vinegar and fresh coriander.
equipment: slotted spoon or ladle for skimming

ingredients.item: dried black beans, rinsed and picked over
cold water, for soaking and cooking
red pepper, finely chopped, plus thin strips to garnish
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover 450 g dried black beans with 2400 ml cold water in a large pot and leave to soak overnight.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Next day, without draining, add 1 tbsp olive oil, the chopped onion, chopped red pepper, crushed garlic and a bay leaf; bring to the boil, then simmer gently for about 1 hour, skimming off any foam.

steps.title: Sofrito
steps.text: In a separate pan, warm 60 ml olive oil and soften the finely chopped onion, pepper and garlic for about 5 minutes, then stir in a bay leaf, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp oregano, 1 tsp pepper and 1½ tsp salt and cook for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Scrape the sofrito into the beans, add 2 tbsp cider vinegar, bring back to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 60-90 minutes, stirring often, until creamy and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Discard both bay leaves, season to taste and stir in 1 tsp sugar off the heat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter with 2 tbsp chopped coriander and pepper strips, and serve over rice or as a soup.

tips: Rinse and pick through the dried beans before soaking to remove any grit or shrivelled beans.
Skim the foam as the beans first come to the boil for a clearer, less bitter pot.
Stir often once the sofrito is in, as the beans thicken and can catch on the base of the pot.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze, and reheat gently on the stove with a splash of water to loosen. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
